assumptions: Hypothesis 1: the GFP reporter is a fourth transcriptional unit whose transcription is driven by the same Hill-type repression function as the repressilator genes, but repressed by TetR (the reporter promoter is PLtetO1, Fig. 1a), with the same promoter strength alpha_g = alpha and the same relative leakiness alpha_g0/alpha_g = 1e-3.

Hypothesis 2: cell growth and division are represented as a first-order dilution term mu*p acting on all protein species (mu = ln2/doubling time, doubling time 60 min taken from the 50-70 min division times reported in the paper); the paper's continuous model omits this term.

Hypothesis 3: the half-lives quoted in the paper (10 min for tagged repressors, 90 min for GFP-aav) are pure degradation rates, so degradation and growth dilution add up; this slightly overestimates total protein loss (the quoted half-lives may already include dilution in vivo).

Hypothesis 4: the same rescaled units as Box 1 are retained (protein in units of K_M = 40 monomers per cell, mRNA divided by translation efficiency, but time kept in minutes so that the period can be compared directly with the measured 160 +/- 40 min).

Hypothesis 5: transcription-only leakiness, Hill-type repression with n = 2, no repressor dimerization, no mRNA dilution term (mRNA lifetime is far shorter than the doubling time), and no GFP maturation step (the finite oxidation rate of GFP is acknowledged as a limitation, not modelled).
Hypothesis 6: total per-cell fluorescence is proportional to p_gfp, i.e. the reporter signal is a linear read-out of the GFP protein level.
description: Hypothesis-driven extension of the published repressilator model (Elowitz & Leibler 2000, Box 1). The core six ODEs are kept, and two mechanisms that the paper describes biologically but never formalises are added: (i) dilution of all protein species by cell growth and division, and (ii) the GFP reporter module (PLtetO1-driven gfp-aav) that provides the experimentally observed fluorescence read-out. Time is expressed in minutes so that the simulated period can be compared directly with the measured 160 +/- 40 min oscillation period. Model question: do sustained oscillations survive growth dilution, and does the slow GFP reporter track the TetR dynamics faithfully?
missing_information: Measured reporter-plasmid promoter strength and copy number: the reporter plasmid is a higher-copy ColE1 plasmid, so alpha_g may differ from alpha; we assume equality.
Absolute calibration between GFP fluorescence (arbitrary units) and GFP molecules per cell is not given, so p_gfp is only a relative read-out.
The rate of GFP chromophore oxidation/maturation is not quantified in the paper.
The division time of MC4100 in the microscopy conditions (50-70 min) is given only as a range.
Initial conditions of the experiments and the exact form of the growth-dilution term (exponential vs linear growth) are not specified.
model_name: Repressilator + GFP reporter readout with growth dilution (self-derived extension of Elowitz & Leibler 2000 Box 1)

assumptions: Hypothesis 1: the GFP reporter is a fourth transcriptional unit whose transcription is driven by the same Hill-type repression function as the repressilator genes, but repressed by TetR (the reporter promoter is PLtetO1, Fig. 1a), with the same promoter strength alpha_g = alpha and the same relative leakiness alpha_g0/alpha_g = 1e-3.

Hypothesis 2: cell growth and division are represented as a first-order dilution term mu*p acting on all protein species (mu = ln2/doubling time, doubling time 60 min taken from the 50-70 min division times reported in the paper); the paper's continuous model omits this term.
Hypothesis 3: the half-lives quoted in the paper (10 min for tagged repressors, 90 min for GFP-aav) are treated as pure degradation rates, so degradation and growth dilution add up.

Hypothesis 4: the same rescaled concentration units as Box 1 are retained (protein in units of K_M = 40 monomers per cell, mRNA divided by translation efficiency), but time is kept in minutes so that period can be compared directly with the measured 160 +/- 40 min.
Hypothesis 5: only the core repressilator parameters are taken from the paper; the GFP module parameters (alpha_g, alpha_g0) and the dilution rate mu are our own assumptions.
Hypothesis 6: per-cell fluorescence is proportional to p_gfp.
origin.source_text: self-derived from Elowitz M.B. & Leibler S., Nature 403, 335-338 (2000) (mechanistic description of the PLtetO1-gfp-aav reporter and of ssrA-tagged, destabilised repressors; growth-dilution mechanism not modelled in the paper)
